newsitem.title: MEXICO: Moderna results buoyed by cigarette sales-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Moderna results buoyed by cigarette sales-analysts.

text.p: Mexico's Empresas La Moderna produced 1996 results mostly in line with market expectations with cigarette sales impressive but the seeds division lagging, analysts said on Tuesday.

The Monterrey-based company on Tuesday reported 1996 net profits of 1.188 billion pesos and operating income of 1.536 billion pesos on sales of 14.319 billion pesos and an earnings per share of 1.96 pesos.
"I thought it (domestic cigarette sales growth) was pretty favorable. It had been kind of struggling the last few quarters," Alyce Andrews, an analyst with Merrill Lynch in New York, told Reuters.
Better still was La Moderna's export sales of cigarettes, up 38 percent to some $47 million.
"They've proven that they are serious about becoming an international player, especially in the Asian market," Scott Wilkins, an analyst with Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Mexico City, told Reuters.
A Reuters survey of four analysts predicted operating income of 1.6 billion on revenues of 13.6 billion pesos and an EPS of 2.17 pesos.

However, analysts said 1996 results were very difficult to predict because of the vast changes in the company, which sold a grain seeds division of one subsidiary, merged a fresh produce subsidiary with another firm, sold two wood products companies and bought a fresh produce distributor.
Encouraging to analysts was the company's reported three percent growth in domestic cigarette sales for the year to maintain its market-share lead of 53 percent.

In addition, La Moderna's packing subsidiary Empaques Ponderosa SA earlier reported a strong 1996 with profits more than doubling from 1995 to 254.72 million pesos while revenues and operating income actually fell.
"We're very bullish on Empaques," Wilkins said. "That's what we'd be buying now."
If there was a downside, it was the agrobiotechnology division, which performed slightly below some expectations.

But one analyst, Georgina Gutierrez of BBV-Probursa in Mexico City, said the operating loss for the seeds division in the fourth quarter was to be expected because of cyclical factors that result in very few sales at the end of the year.
"We still think the share price is in good shape and we are maintaining our hold recommendation," Gutierrez told Reuters.
La Moderna's A shares closed down 10 centavos to 40.90 pesos on Tuesday.
